data.name: Gangaadhar
data.gender_notes: Gangaadhar is used as a male name in Hindu naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Gangaadhar refers to the one who carries the river Ganga on his head. This name is derived from the Sanskrit words 'Ganga' meaning river and 'Adhara' meaning carrier. In Hindu mythology, Lord Shiva is the embodiment of Gangaadhar, as he holds the river Ganga on his head. The name Gangaadhar carries the meaning “God's carrier” and is chosen by families in Hindu traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Sanskrit tradition and is also used in Hindi, Sanskrit, Marathi. Parents who choose Gangaadhar usually hope their child will grow to embody god's carrier and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: Symbolizes the inner strength and selflessness, carrying the burdens of others.
data.etymology: Gangaadhar belongs to the Sanskrit linguistic tradition and is used in Hindu naming. Its recorded meaning is “God's carrier.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Gangaadhar total 8, giving a life-path number of 8. Number 8 is linked with Saturn and with the qualities of ambition, resilience and material success.

data.cultural_impact: The name Gangaadhar holds great cultural significance in Hinduism, as it resonates with the profound love and devotion towards the river Ganga, which is considered sacred and pure. It symbolizes Lord Shiva's dedication to maintaining the purity and nourishment of the river for the countless generations.
data.spiritual_significance: On a spiritual level, the name Gangaadhar represents the concept of serving and carrying the divine will, much like Lord Shiva carrying the river Ganga. It can be interpreted as a reminder to carry the burden of the universe and its beings with pure intention, selflessness, and devotion, just as Lord Shiva does. Ultimately, this name urges us to become embodiments of such devotion and sacrifice, both personally and collectively.
data.spiritual_symbolism: Gangaadhar symbolizes the divine grace of the Ganga River, embodied in a protector or bearer. This name signifies the strength and purity of the river, bestowing its blessings upon its bearer.

historical_references.reference: Gangaadhar was a king of the Maurya dynasty, ruling from around 320-305 BCE. He is known for his military campaigns that expanded the Mauryan Empire into the south, as far as the Godavari River.

Another Gangaadhar is mentioned in the 12th century Indian epic 'Mahabharata'. In this context, he was a prince of the Panchala Kingdom, having a significant role in the great battle of Kurukshetra between the Pandava and Kaurava princes.

modern_usage.modern_context: The name 'Gangaadhar' is derived from the Hindu mythology, where Lord Ganga is depicted as carrying Lord Shiva on her head. This name is popularly used as a given name in the Indian subcontinent. In the modern context, the name 'Gangaadhar' is seen on various platforms such as social media, entertainment industry, and the tech industry. On social media, individuals with the name 'Gangaadhar' can be found sharing content related to Indian culture, Hindu deities, and mythology. In the entertainment industry, 'Gangaadhar' has been used as the title of a 2015 Indian film that revolves around a blind man who gains his sight after touching the idol of Lord Gangaadhar. In the tech industry, 'Gangaadhar' is the name of an open-source machine learning library developed by the Indian Institute of Technology Kharagpur. The name 'Gangaadhar' is also used as a username or handle on various social media platforms and online communities, reflecting the deep connection and interest of individuals in Indian culture, Hindu deities, and mythology.

name_in_real_life.story: A devoted individual named Krishna Gangaadhar in Kathmandu, Nepal attributes much of their spiritual journey to their name Gangaadhar, which means "God's carrier". They believe their name has guided them on the path of righteousness.
